doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

chapter: Early New Orleans experiences and sideman roles
title: Adapting as a sideman: faux stride and Boney James
summary: He plays stride with Evan Christopher, keyboards with Boney James, and silent movies.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: That sounds great. You mentioned sort of an aside, like well I’m not a great stride player and here I am playing with Evan Christopher.
Yeah he puts up with my faux stride.
Your faux stride. But as a working musician you have to adapt constantly, especially if you’re in the role of a sideman.

Sure. When I played keyboards with Boney James there was no stride to be had — you didn’t need stride. I just needed sounds, and you know, understanding that he is not a bebopper. But his first influence was Grover and the great musicians in that smooth jazz world like Kirk Whalum. I mean all these wonderful musicians that are playing in an artificial format but it’s just funk music, it’s just an instrumental pop music is all it is. And so as a New Orleans musician I’ve played many different styles. I’ve played piano for silent movies. You know, just different things. And it’s all fun. It’s all great.
